messages:
asha: seeing a bunch of NCCL TIMEOUT / "peer reset" during a multi-GPU training job on eu-west-gpu-3 cluster. Job retries, then hangs. :grimacing:

mikko: can you paste the nccl error snippet? also which kernel + driver?

asha: here's the tail from the job: 
```
NCCL WARN Net/Plugin : Connection to rank 2 failed, peer reset
NCCL ERROR net/ib : Couldn't connect, aborting
NCCL INFO Finalize
```
Running nvidia-driver 535.86.05, kernel 6.1.76. GPUs are A100s.

lina: I noticed a switch syslog alert around the same time: "port 48 flapped on TOR-7; link up/down 3x in 10s". Could be east-west link instability.

devon: digging into host logs, /var/log/messages shows mlx5_core reporting "mlx5_core 0000:5e:00.0: Port 1 link down" and back up. Also saw a lot of UDP fragments dropped by kernel: "IPV4: UDP: checksum failed" interleaved.

asha: our workload uses RoCEv2 (UDP) + GPUDirect RDMA. If UDP fragments get dropped NCCL sees peer disconnects.

mikko: can you run ethtool + ibv_devinfo on the affected node and paste? particularly mtu + tso/gro/gro settings on the bond and the switch MTU (jumbo?).

lina: pulled outputs quickly: 
```
# ethtool -k eth0
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
tcp-segmentation-offload: on
udp-fragmentation-offload: off
generic-segmentation-offload: on
generic-receive-offload: on

# ip link show bond0
3: bond0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
```

And ibv_devinfo: 
```
hca_id: mlx5_0
transport: InfiniBand (0)
phys_port_cnt: 2
link_layer: Ethernet
max_mtu: 4096
active_mtu: 2048
```

devon: switch team confirms some TORs still set to MTU 9216 but active path to this rack has MTU 9000 on some intermediate devices. Could be a fragmentation boundary causing RoCEv2 to split/fragment and some fragments dropped by offload/firmware mismatch.

ops-oncall: quick repro checklist: reduce batch -> smaller packet sizes to avoid fragmentation, or force host MTU to 2048 temporarily to see if stable. Also try disabling GSO/GRO to see if host offload is corrupting checksums.

asha: tried disabling GRO/TCP/TSO on the bond: 
```
ethtool -K bond0 gro off gso off tso off
```
Restarted job, still saw sporadic peer reset but frequency dropped.

mikko: that suggests combination of offload + MTU mismatch + intermittent link flaps. We should also check PFC/priority flow control on the fabric; if PFC is misconfigured you'll see pause frames and microbursts causing drops for RoCE traffic.

lina: switch config snippet (redacted): 
```
interface Ethernet48
  mtu 9216
  priority-flow-control 3 on
  spanning-tree edge-port
```
Intermediate aggregation device had PFC disabled.

devon: opened a ticket with net-team: NET-8472 (high) to standardize MTU + PFC across leaf->agg->tor for RoCE lanes. For immediate workaround I spun the job onto nodes in a rack where tor/agg MTU/PFC are consistent (rack-12). That job finished normally.

infra-bot: deploy-alert: live-job migration triggered for training job id 0x7f3c at 1902345658 by dev-scheduler.

asha: good catch. Plan: 1) net-team to align MTU/PFC, 2) infra to add an MTU/PFC health probe to capacity checks, 3) devex to document RoCE lane requirements.

mikko: also adding a short-term nccl fallback: set environment var NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME to exclude the problematic bond (e.g., NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eno2) or set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 to use TCP as last resort for critical runs.

lina: I'll run a sweep across eu-west pools to list nodes where active_mtu != 4096 or bond mtu != switch mtu and send to NET-8472.

asha: thanks everyone. Leaving this thread open for the NET ticket updates. :thumbsup:
